title: Filesystem blocks versus inodes
summary: Understand why a filesystem can reject writes when capacity or inode availability is exhausted.

concepts.title: Block capacity
concepts.explanation: File contents and filesystem metadata consume allocated storage blocks.

concepts.title: Inode capacity
concepts.explanation: Many files can exhaust inode-like metadata even when block capacity remains.

concepts.title: Open deleted files
concepts.explanation: A removed pathname can continue consuming storage while a process keeps the file open.

limitations: High usage does not identify which files or process caused growth.
Filesystem reporting and reserved capacity vary by filesystem and privilege.
